I opened the source: it is Facebook's own transcript of its Q1 2019 earnings call, dated April 24th, 2019. The quoted words are on it exactly. They come from Zuckerberg's answer to Colin Sebastian (Baird). The analyst asked how much harmful-content blocking can be done with AI, and Zuckerberg began his answer by saying "the only hope is building AI systems that can either identify things and handle them proactively". This is a transcript of the call, not a news report.

How it reads against the four parts:
1. **Role: passes.** He was Facebook's founder and chief executive, and Facebook ran FAIR from 2013. The ledger already counts this role for his earlier claims (the 2016 and 2018 files).
2. **Forward-looking and about AI: passes.** The forecast is about what share of removed harmful content Facebook's AI systems flag before users report it. That is a statement about what AI will do. His hedge ("my hope would be") stays in the wording of the prediction.
3. **A date or length of time: borderline.** The main forecast, 90-plus percent "within the next couple of years", depends on "a couple of years". The rulings say "a few years" is undated, but none covers "a couple". It may mean two years, which would be due in 2021, or it may be as loose as "a few". By the rule, a truly borderline case stays out and is logged. The same sentence also contains a clearly dated "will not" forecast: "certainly not in the next six months or a year" for 99 percent in every category. Under reading 2 that part could be scored on its own, due 2020-04-24 at the later end of the span. It is not the claim the search run put forward, though, and the reviewer may want to look at it separately.
4. **Primary source: passes.** It is the company's own transcript.

**Already recorded? No.** The closest file, 2018-04-10-zuckerberg-hate-speech-ai-five-to-ten-years, is a different claim: hate speech only, with a five-to-ten-year span, said a year earlier.
